title: Sustainability and Carbon Accounting

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Collecting Emissions Data
children.blurb: Collecting emissions data means gathering the raw measurements and activity records that let an organization calculate its greenhouse gas footprint across scope 1, scope 2, and scope 3 categories.

children.name: Checking Claims Against the Ledger
children.blurb: Checking claims against the ledger means comparing public sustainability and carbon statements, such as net zero pledges or emissions reductions, with the underlying accounting records and transactional data that support them.

children.name: Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data
children.blurb: Combining financial and non-financial data means bringing together traditional accounting figures, such as revenue, capital expenditure, and operating costs, with sustainability metrics like greenhouse gas emissions, water use, and workforce demographics.

children.name: Drafting Sustainability Disclosures
children.blurb: This page covers the use of AI to draft sustainability disclosures, including greenhouse gas emissions reports, climate risk narratives, and governance statements.

children.name: Carbon Credit Records
children.blurb: Carbon credit records are the structured documentation of verified emissions reductions or removals, including issuance, ownership, transfer, retirement, and any associated project data.

sections.body: Sustainability and carbon accounting here means the work of turning scattered emissions and energy records into numbers that can be checked, combined with financial data, and written into disclosures. Artificial intelligence is doing this now by reading utility bills, invoices, sensor logs, and supplier reports, then extracting figures like kilowatt hours, fuel volumes, and tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. It matches those extracted figures to the categories used in reporting standards, such as scope 1, scope 2, and scope 3 emissions. It also compares a company's stated emissions against the underlying records it can access, flags gaps or double counting, and drafts plain language summaries for regulatory filings. For carbon credits, AI systems maintain records of issuance, transfer, and retirement, and check that a credit has not been used more than once.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The solved parts are narrow. AI reliably extracts numbers from standard invoice and meter formats, and it can reconcile totals when the underlying data is already structured and labeled. It can also generate first drafts of disclosure text from a set of approved figures. What is not solved is verification of physical emissions. AI cannot measure what a factory actually released, it can only check whether reported numbers are consistent with the records it has. Carbon credit quality remains a hard problem because the underlying project claims, such as avoided deforestation, are often not machine checkable. Honest limits include fragmented reporting standards, missing supplier data, and the fact that many emissions figures are estimates rather than measurements. A human still has to confirm that the right boundaries were used and that the records are complete.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Collecting Emissions Data to see how raw utility and supplier records are turned into a single emissions ledger. From there, Checking Claims Against the Ledger shows how reported figures are compared with that ledger to find mismatches or unsupported claims. Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data explains how emissions totals are placed next to revenue, capital expenditure, and other financial line items for integrated reports. Drafting Sustainability Disclosures covers the step of turning those combined figures into narrative and tabular text that meets a given reporting framework. Carbon Credit Records is where a reader goes to understand how credits are tracked from issuance to retirement and how double counting is checked. The site tracks 432 company pages, so a reader can move from any company page to these five pages to see how that company's reported sustainability data would be handled.
